World.title: Quiet Inheritance: Why the Croatian Diaspora Should Seek Citizenship For Their Children
World.content:
August the 19th, 2026 – Even if you don’t plan to open a business, move, or do anything concrete, as a member of the Croatian diaspora, gaining citizenship could mean the gateway to EU education and career opportunities for generations to come.

For a growing number of American parents who happen to have Croatian ancestry, the decision to pursue Croatian citizenship is no longer mainly about their own travel plans or personal connection to the country. It’s about their children…

eu citizenship is about so much more than getting through the border more quickly…

Across the United States, parents are quietly assembling birth certificates and family records. Maybe they were fuelled by the sense of sweeping national pride the World Cup brought, or maybe the fact that that burdensome double taxation treaty between the USA and Croatia is on its way to being scrapped. Maybe it’s none of that. It could be a desire to reconnect with the roots of their ancestors as a nod to all they went through for better lives across the Atlantic Ocean.

Whatever the reason behind the move, the end goal of such a move is relatively straightforward – to secure Croatian citizenship. Even if there are zero plans to move to Croatia or anywhere else in the EU, start up a business, move a company to the EU or retire, holding Croatian (and thus EU) citizenship means that their sons and daughters can also do the same, automatically gaining full EU rights. That of course includes unfettered access to higher education and unrestricted work opportunities across 27 different countries.

This isn’t just another theoretical benefit. Once a parent becomes a Croatian citizen through descent, minor children can typically acquire the same citizenship with far less complexity involved. That single step creates a permanent legal pathway that remains open for the next generation, regardless of whether the family ever relocates.

a european education with zero barriers

One of the clearest practical advantages is university access. EU citizens generally pay the same tuition rates as local students at public universities throughout most of the European Union. In many countries those fees are substantially lower than the costs American students face at home, and in some cases they approach zero for EU nationals. Holding a Croatian passport also removes the need for student visas or complex sponsorship arrangements when applying to programmes in Germany, the Netherlands, Austria, Ireland, or other member states. Students can move freely for short courses, semester exchanges, or full degree programmes. The Erasmus network and similar mobility schemes become far more accessible when the student already holds EU citizenship rather than relying on temporary permissions.

For families watching American college costs rise astronomically year after year, this represents a concrete parallel option. It doesn’t require abandoning American universities. It simply expands the menu of realistic choices available to a teenager who holds both an American and a Croatian passport. It is also far easier on the pockets of parents who may only just be making ends meet.

career mobility following graduation – eu wide

The advantages continue after university is over and those famous photos are taken with diplomas in hand. An EU citizen can accept a job offer in any member state without needing a work permit or employer sponsorship. That flexibility matters in competitive fields where companies increasingly recruit across borders. Young dual citizens can take internships in Zagreb or just across the border in Ljubljana, accept graduate roles in Berlin or Amsterdam, or return home to the United States with the knowledge that EU opportunities remain permanently available to them whenever they get the itch to experience them.

Parents who secure the status of Croatian citizens while their children are still minors effectively hand them a form of professional insurance that is extremely difficult to obtain later in life. Rules can (and do) change. You only need to ask the Italian diaspora about the hurdles they now face in what was once an easy ride in getting Italian citizenship. Documentation becomes harder to locate and do anything with as older relatives pass away and time marches on. Completing the process now removes those future variables entirely and ensures flexibility that can hardly be matched in any other manner.

multi-generational safety

Many American parents with Croatian heritage say they have no intention of moving to Europe themselves. Nor do they need to. That’s totally irrelevant to the value of having Croatian citizenship for the next generation. The rights exist whether or not anyone relocates anywhere else. A family can remain fully based in the United States while still giving their children the legal ability to study, work, or live anywhere in the EU if they later choose to do so.

The same logic applies to grandchildren. Citizenship acquired today can, at least under current rules, be transmitted further down the line, creating a multi-generational safety net that requires just one single successful application at the starting point.

timing matters…

The administrative process for Croatian citizenship by descent is (in)famously document-heavy. Birth, marriage, and death records must be gathered, apostilled, and translated… The list goes on. That goes without even mentioning that much older records from the former Yugoslavia or earlier periods can take time to locate and deal with administratively. Consular and ministry processing times currently range from several months to well over a year depending on the complexity of the file.

Parents who begin while their own parents or grandparents are still able to help locate family documents often find the process smoother. Waiting until a child is already applying to universities can leave too little time for the citizenship to be finalised. For American families with verifiable Croatian ancestry, the window remains totally open. There is (at least for now) still no generational cutoff for eligible descendants in most descent-based cases, and dual citizenship with the United States is entirely permitted. The practical question is simply whether the family wants those EU education and mobility rights locked in for the next generation while the paperwork is still manageable.

The decision is less about returning to Croatia, less about business and investments, and more about giving children a permanent set of options that most of their American peers will never have. In an era of rising education costs and increasingly mobile careers, that quiet inheritance is proving more valuable than many families initially expected.

how croatianbydescent.com can help you get your hands on that trusty little blue passport

Croatian by Descent helps the diaspora to take that first step into the (sometimes choppy) waters of gaining Croatian citizenship. It acts as a complete guide to everything you might need to keep in mind when applying or just seeking more information. For total beginners with little to no knowledge of how administrative processes work in Croatia, this can be an invaluable source of guidance throughout the entire process.

Booking a free consultation with Croatian by Descent can set you on the path to securing Croatian and EU citizenship for yourself, thus making travelling to Croatia and Schengen for holidays easy and stress-free. It can also be a priceless gift to your children and grandchildren should they decide to take the leap (even temporarily) back to the country your ancestors left long ago, to attend higher education or to work, opening up a world of incredible opportunities that aren’t on the table for everyone.

World.title: Business Owners and Landlords Seek Relief After Fire in Omiš
World.content:
August the 19th, 2026 – Business owners and private landlords are seeking relief and compensation after the fire that has ravaged the Omiš area.

The well known association Glas poduzetnika (UGP – Voice of Entrepreneurs) has proposed that the Croatian Government adopt an emergency package of measures that would temporarily relieve entrepreneurs affected by the fire in the Omiš area of tax, tourism, chamber and local charges.

Poslovni reports that the association believes that assistance must not be limited only to those whose facilities physically burned down, because damage in the affected area is also suffered by those whose facilities remained intact but who, because of the fire, were left without guests, access, income or the possibility of regular business operations.

“Such a package of assistance should not have to be reinvented every time. Croatia needs a predefined model of automatic relief and assistance to the economy in the event of fires, floods, earthquakes and other major disasters. When a catastrophe occurs, entrepreneurs must know what they can expect, and the state what it must do – without months of waiting for special decisions,” states UGP, which joined the request for urgent assistance at the initiative of the association Spasimo male obiteljske iznajmljivače – SMOi (Let’s Save Small Family Landlords).

They, for their part, are demanding exemption from payment of tax and other charges at least until the end of 2026, while for 2027 they are asking that the need to continue these measures be reassessed according to the actual situation and the speed of recovery of the affected area, noting that “one cannot expect a family from whom the fire has taken the season and income to continue paying the state as if nothing had happened.”

It should also be added that the Zagreb City Administration has announced that Zagreb will donate 130 thousand euros in aid to Omiš.

World.title: Extreme Weather Inflicts Damage on Croatian Tourism and Agriculture
World.content:
August the 19th, 2026 – Extreme weather is damaging Croatian tourism and agriculture, with temperatures above 30 degrees lasting more than a month, the economic cost amounts to around one percent of GDP.

Extreme heat is becoming an increasingly significant economic risk, and Croatia could be among the more exposed European countries due to the structure of its economy. In addition to the usual summer heat, summer is the season in which temperatures are rising the fastest, the State Hydrometeorological Institute (DHMZ) revealed. Poslovni reports that from 1961 to 2020, the average summer temperature increased by between 0.3 and 0.6°C per decade, depending on the area.

In the same period, a significant increase was recorded in the number of warm days – days with a maximum daily temperature of at least 25°C – locally by up to 8.3 days per decade. “Climate change therefore does not simply mean less or more rain, but changes the timing, frequency and intensity of precipitation, and with it the associated risks,” DHMZ said. According to empirical findings for 35 countries, every additional degree above 30°C reduces labour productivity by around three percent.

risks to businesses

For companies, extreme weather conditions are no longer just a matter of meteorology or public health, but an increasingly concrete business risk. Extreme heat for some employers means fewer working hours, lower productivity, higher costs, pressure on agricultural yields and growing costs of adapting to new weather conditions. Heat thus becomes a risk that, unlike damage after a flood or storm, is often not immediately visible.

“Extreme heat creates significant business costs for European companies. According to relevant analyses, the share of lost working hours due to heat stress could rise from 1.4 percent in 1995 to 2.2–2.5 percent by 2030. According to empirical findings for 35 countries, every additional degree above 30°C reduces labour productivity by around three percent (1.3 dollars in purchasing power parity per hour of work). Among European economies, the largest drop in productivity is estimated for France, Italy and Slovenia, and Croatia does not deviate much from that trio.

In the short term, the largest part of the cost is borne by companies because wages do not decrease despite the drop in productivity, which reduces profit margins. An additional negative effect comes from warmer nights, which in 2024 caused a record 8.7 percent more lost sleep, further worsening the productivity of office workers as well,” said Hrvoje Stojić, chief economist at the Croatian Employers’ Association (HUP).

Stojić points out that in general the estimates hold that in the case of 30 or more days with temperatures above 30 degrees Celsius, the economic cost amounts to around one percent of GDP.

“What is particularly worrying is the fact that climate risks are no longer the exception, which is why they are increasingly becoming part of regular business planning. Every day of production interruption, logistics disruption or reduced employee productivity due to extreme conditions represents a direct financial cost,” said Marija Šćulac, vice-president of the Croatian Chamber of Economy (HGK). “Croatia is among the countries that are particularly exposed to climate risks, especially due to the size of its economy and the structure of the economy.

According to World Bank estimates from 2025, Croatia will need additional investments amounting to around 1.1 percent of GDP annually for successful adaptation to climate change and decarbonisation, while it is emphasised that delaying adaptation will be more expensive in the long run than timely investments. That is why we now view climate change as a matter of managing business risks,” she added. Šćulac says that the sectors most exposed to higher costs due to high temperatures are those that depend on natural conditions or are energy-intensive. Agriculture is already facing the consequences of droughts and heavy rainfall that directly reduce yields.

This is also confirmed by data from the Ministry of Agriculture. The Strategic Study for the Agriculture Strategy states that high temperatures, droughts and large amounts of precipitation negatively affect agricultural production. In addition, when maximum daily temperatures above 30°C last for more than ten consecutive days, agricultural crops enter a state of heat stress and stop growing.

In agriculture, climate risk is first seen in yields, but for Croatia its broader economic consequences could be significantly greater in tourism. According to the European Commission Report for Croatia, the direct contribution to GDP is 11.8 percent, the highest among member states, while tourism-related sectors generate around a quarter of gross value added.

risks to tourism

“Due to high temperatures, guests are changing their habits and we can expect fewer of them to come during the hottest summer months. This means that the tourism sector will have to adapt its business models to the new climate circumstances and year-round tourism. Major challenges also await the construction sector, which must find a way to organise work on construction sites during extreme heat, while logistics and transport are already feeling the consequences of disruptions caused by droughts and low water levels,” Šćulac said.

8.7 percent is what the decline in productivity stood at back in 2024 due to warmer nights. Such a development could be particularly important for Croatia, whose tourism is strongly concentrated in the summer months. The European Environment Agency warns that climate change may affect the seasonality and geographical distribution of tourist demand also because of the growing risk of extreme heat.

“Paradoxically, the sector that is key to the transition is itself highly vulnerable. The energy sector is under pressure because droughts reduce hydropower production precisely when consumption is highest. That is why it is important to develop a balanced energy mix that includes renewable sources, but also – and this is crucial – a strong and modern electricity grid that will be able to accommodate an ever-increasing number of renewable energy sources. Since extreme weather conditions affect almost all sectors, the focus is on how ready each individual sector is to manage climate risks. Companies that invest in energy efficiency, digitalisation, their own renewable energy sources and resilient infrastructure will in the long run be more competitive than those that postpone adaptation,” Šćulac said.

Examples of the impact on logistics can be found everywhere, and the Dutch one stands out in particular because the Port of Rotterdam, as the largest and one of the most important, connects maritime traffic with river, rail and road transport and enables the distribution of goods in Europe. Cargo ships transporting chemicals, oil and other goods to and from Rotterdam can, due to low water levels, be loaded only to about 30 percent of capacity in order to prevent grounding, the Financial Times reported. This means that carriers have to pay for around 100 additional river cargo ships (barges) per week, yet still cannot transport the full quantity of goods as before the drought.

The World Bank in its 2025 report for Croatia estimates that, without additional action, climate events covered by their model alone could reduce Croatian GDP by up to 2.1 percent by 2050, with infrastructure, tourism and agriculture being particularly affected.

World.title: New Croatian Toll Collection: Here’s What You Need to Know
World.content:
August the 19th, 2026 – The new Croatian motorway toll collection system will alter things as we know them quite dramatically. Here’s everything you need to know.

Poslovni reports that the new Croatian toll collection project covers the entire Croatian motorway network, including the motorways managed by Croatian Motorways, Bina Istra and the Zagreb–Macelj Motorway, meaning that Croatia should (for the first time ever) get a unified electronic toll collection system. Croatian Motorways are currently preparing one of the biggest changes in the way tolls are collected in recent decades. Classic toll booths are expected to become a thing of the past, and the new system will allow drivers to pass through motorways without stopping.

For the many drivers who already use ENC, the immediate question is: what will happen to their device? The good news is that ENC is not disappearing. On the contrary, it will remain one of the two basic methods of payment in the new system. The system will use free-flow vehicle technology, or Multi-Lane Free Flow, so it will no longer be necessary to slow down and stop in front of a barrier, tportal reports.

For passenger cars there will be two options. Drivers will be able to continue using their ENC device, while vehicles without one will be recognised by the system through automatic reading of licence plates. For heavy vehicles, ENC will be mandatory. This means that existing ENC users will not have to give up their device just because the toll booths are disappearing. What is primarily changing is the way the infrastructure will register the passage of vehicles.

The biggest change will be precisely the absence of physical barriers. Instead of approaching a barrier, slowing down and waiting, the vehicle will pass through the toll zone in the normal flow of traffic, and the system will automatically record the passage.

HAC states that tolls will continue to be calculated according to the distance travelled and the vehicle category, as is the case today. The goal of the new system is to reduce congestion, travel time, fuel consumption and emissions caused by slowing down and waiting at toll stations. The project covers the entire Croatian motorway network, including the motorways managed by Croatian Motorways, Bina Istra and the Zagreb–Macelj Motorway, so Croatia should for the first time get a unified electronic toll collection system.

An additional sign of the transition is already visible. At the beginning of July, HAC announced the gradual abolition of ARZ SMART cards, with the possibility of transferring funds to an ENC account. From the 1st of October 2026, SMART cards will no longer be usable for paying tolls. For the average driver, the most important message is therefore simple: ENC is not retiring together with the toll booths. In the new system it should become even more practical, because reading will be possible without stopping in front of a barrier.

World.title: Iraq, World Bank discuss new loan to rebuild power grid
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – The Iraqi Ministry of Electricity and the World Bank are discussing a new loan to rebuild and optimize Iraq’s heavily strained national power grid.

Iraqi Electricity Minister Ali Saad Wahib met on Wednesday with Emmanuel Salinas Munoz, the World Bank’s Country Director for Iraq, to evaluate the status of projects carried out under the existing loan and discuss priority projects recommended for inclusion in the new loan.

According to a statement from the Electricity Ministry, the meeting focused on priority projects designed to eliminate bottlenecks in the electrical transmission system and enhance network efficiency. Additionally, the discussion included projects related to gas supplies and the electrical interconnection with Gulf countries.

Wahib indicated that it is important to fund projects that will have a positive impact on developing the power sector’s infrastructure, which would help the ministry raise system efficiency and supply levels.

Iraq’s electricity grid is experiencing a daily shortage of over 35,000 megawatts due to restricted fuel availability for power plants and a reduction in some external supply sources. In early August, output was barely 24,600 megawatts.

Demand in the summer fluctuates between 55,000 and 60,000 megawatts, exacerbating the supply imbalance and causing continued operational issues for the system. Production levels rely on gas supplies from Iran, which stand at around 20 million cubic meters per day.

The Iraqi government is counting on both maintaining current capacity and implementing new generating projects to assure a more steady supply during peak summer demand and prevent power outages.

World.title: What’s behind the UAE’s decision to cut Iran trade ties?
World.content:
Dubai – The UAE this week announced suspending trade with Iran, heaping pressure on its major trading partner at the same time that the US declared “economic warfare” on Tehran.

It is unclear when the ban came into place and what has prompted it, with the UAE citing “regional escalations”.

Experts have said that the UAE is sending a message to Iran, which has ramped up attacks on Emirati tankers in the Strait of Hormuz, while also signalling alignment with the United States — although halting trade is expected to do little in the way of curbing illicit flows.

– How was UAE-Iran trade? –

The United Arab Emirates is a significant trading partner for Iran and its top import country.

In the 10 months preceding the war, Iran’s trade with the UAE totalled $21 billion according to official Iranian figures.

In 2024, Iran relied on the UAE for 30.6 percent of its imports totalling roughly $21 billion according to the World Trade Organization.

The UAE is also Iran’s third largest export destination, making up 12 percent of its exports, totalling more than $7 billion.

The vast majority of UAE trade with Iran consists in re-exports, according to official Emirati data, including everything from phones to meat and other food.

These figures do not take into account smuggling and illicit flows, which are difficult to assess.

Some Trump allies have lauded the UAE’s efforts, hoping it will help stifle Iran’s economy.

– Will it curb illicit flows? –

But halting licit flows may have little impact on Iran’s sanctions evasion network.

Experts have said that Iran uses UAE banks and its financial system to access the world economy through illicit, often murky transactions.

“Billions of dollars of the regime’s sanctioned oil revenue moves through UAE by way of opaque shell companies based in China/Hong Kong,” according to Max Meizlish, a researcher at the Foundation for Defense of Democracies (FDD) think tank.

He formerly worked for the US Department of the Treasury’s Office of Foreign Assets Control (OFAC), responsible for sanctions.

“That means halting all direct trade, commercial exchange, and financial transactions with Iran may still allow billions in oil revenue to reach the regime indirectly,” he said.

“UAE deserves credit for this long overdue move, but the US needs to keep up the pressure and ensure banks in the Emirates apply enhanced due diligence on transactions for which there is reason to suspect possible Iranian sanctions evasion/shadow banking.”

– Why now? –

The UAE took a hawkish stance on Iran in the early weeks of the war, recalling its ambassador in Tehran and shutting schools and hospitals linked to the Iranian state that it said violated its laws.

But since the signing of a memorandum of understanding between the United States and Iran in June, an understanding appeared to take shape.

Iran, which had unleashed the bulk of its wrath on the UAE in the first round of war, did not launch attacks aimed at the country since May.

The UAE announcement coincided with a campaign by its US ally to inflict economic pain on Iran as the war nears its sixth month with no immediate diplomatic or military off-ramp in sight.

One day after the UAE announcement, US President Donald Trump said he was launching a major new campaign to target Iran’s economy.

For Esfandyar Batmanghelidj, who heads the Bourse & Bazaar Foundation, the UAE has not changed its Iran strategy, but it is under US pressure to contribute to the US economic sanctions campaign.

Their statement is a way of “publicly signalling that there is no daylight between the US and UAE positions”.

Iran has also been hitting ADNOC tankers repeatedly in the past weeks and the UAE recently reported Iranian missiles targeting shipping that fell in the water, after earlier saying they were directed at the country.

For Emirati researcher Mohammed Baharoon, who heads the Dubai Public Policy Research Center, the UAE move comes “after various attempts to reconnect Iran after the war”.

“This is not about joining the US sanction (effort) but about re-establishing the basis of the relationship. Iran can’t ask for connectivity while they are blocking it,” he added, in reference to their attacks on Emirati tankers.

World.title: Iraq’s parliament speaker fires back at Iran with ‘Arabian Gulf’ post
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) — Iraqi Parliament Speaker Haibat al-Halbousi shared a photograph of himself on Thursday in front of a map labeled “Arabian Gulf,” in apparent reaction to Iranian Parliament Speaker Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf’s exhibition of the same body of water as the “Persian Gulf.”

Al-Halbousi tweeted the photograph on his X account with simply the Arabic hashtag #الخليج_العربي — #Arabian_Gulf, turning a longstanding regional nomenclature issue into a sharp interaction between the Iraqi and Iranian parliament speakers.

The timing of the post is very noteworthy.

Just one day earlier, al-Halbousi met with Ghalibaf in Baghdad as part of the Iranian official’s high-level visit to Iraq, where they discussed bilateral ties, economic cooperation, and regional developments.

During the meetings, al-Halbousi also asked Iran to grant Iraq special consideration for oil shipments via the Strait of Hormuz, highlighting the economic harm caused by regional tensions and interruptions to the crucial waterway.

Ghalibaf’s visit comes at an especially tense time in Iraq-Iran relations.

Baghdad is aiming to maintain connections with Tehran while still under intense US pressure over Iran-aligned armed forces and pursuing closer economic and security ties with Saudi Arabia, other Gulf nations, and Washington.

The dueling map postings therefore have much more political symbolism than a simple debate over nomenclature.

Iran has long insisted on the moniker “Persian Gulf,” but Iraq and the Arab Gulf nations typically prefer “Arabian Gulf.” The word has regularly sparked diplomatic difficulties in the area.

The Iranian Consulate in Najaf then joined in on the subject, reiterating Iran’s historical stance on the Persian Gulf moniker, adding to what had started as a social-media conversation between high political officials.

For Baghdad, however, al-Halbousi’s statement might also be considered an affirmation of Iraq’s unique Arab identity and autonomous political stance at a time when Tehran’s influence inside the nation is under increased scrutiny.

The incident is especially noteworthy since al-Halbousi had maintained direct contact with Iran at the same time.

During Wednesday’s meeting, he urged closer parliamentary cooperation with Tehran while emphasizing the need for protecting Iraq’s economic interests, notably its capacity to export oil via Hormuz.

Iraq has also grown closer to its Arab neighbors.

Last month, Al-Halbousi met with the secretary-general of the Gulf Cooperation Council in Baghdad, emphasizing Iraq’s commitment to developing cooperation with Arab Gulf nations in economic, political, and security areas.

The debate emphasizes the increasingly difficult balancing act that Iraq faces.

Baghdad wants cordial relations with neighboring Iran, but it also seeks better integration with the Arab Gulf, improved contacts with Washington, and more control over Iran-aligned armed organizations operating inside the nation.

Against this environment, a single word on a map has gained political significance.

Less than 24 hours after sitting across the table from Ghalibaf in Baghdad, Iraq’s parliament speaker made his own terms abundantly clear: Arabian Gulf.

World.title: Barca seal Cancelo return to bolster defence
World.content:
Barcelona – Barcelona have signed defender Joao Cancelo on a free transfer, the Spanish champions said Thursday.

“The full-back arrives as a free agent and signs on until June 30, 2029,” said Barca in a statement.

Portugal international Cancelo terminated his contract with Saudi Arabian side Al Hilal in order to return to Camp Nou.

The 32-year-old has previously spent two loan spells with Barca, including in the second half of last season, helping Hansi Flick’s side retain La Liga.

Cancelo played in Portugal, Spain and Italy before joining Manchester City in 2019.

The defender was loaned to Bayern Munich and then Barcelona in the 2023/24 campaign before joining Al Hilal in 2024.

Cancelo follows Rodri, Anthony Gordon and Karim Adeyemi to Barca this summer, with the Catalan giants still looking to sign a striker after the departures of Robert Lewandowski and Ferran Torres.

Barca were hoping to sign Atletico Madrid’s Julian Alvarez but have to look elsewhere with the Rojiblancos refusing to let the Argentina international move.

Flick’s team begin their La Liga campaign on Sunday at Elche.

World.title: Germany reports record 14,000 heat-related deaths this summer
World.content:
Frankfurt – Germany registered a record of around 14,000 heat-related deaths this summer as Europe struggled through a series of punishing heatwaves, official data showed Thursday.

Around 9,600 of those deaths were recorded in one week in late June when Germany baked in temperatures of over 40C, according to the Robert Koch Institute.

The heatwaves and drought have fuelled a historically hot summer in Europe, contributing to a spike in heat-related mortality in the worst-hit countries.

Spain’s public health institute registered nearly 4,500 heat-related deaths since June 1, figures showed Thursday. French health authorities said they had seen more than 7,300 excess deaths over the same period.

In Germany, the largest share of heat-related deaths occurred in the over-75 age group, the public health authority said in a statement.

“In some cases — such as heatstroke — exposure to heat leads directly to death, whereas in most instances, death results from a combination of heat exposure and pre-existing medical conditions,” said its report.

“Consequently, heat is not usually listed as the underlying cause of death on the death certificate; instead, statistical methods must be employed to estimate the extent of heat-related deaths.”

The institute said it has collected such heat mortality data for the past decade and that the previous record was 8,900 heat-related deaths in 2018. A separate report by a medical publication had estimated 10,000 heat deaths in 1994.

In some years, heat deaths had dropped below 2,000, said the report, adding that “these differences can be attributed to the varying severity of the heatwaves”.

This summer, heat and drought have battered Europe’s biggest economy, also fuelling wildfires, reducing crop yields and dropping water levels in major rivers used for cargo shipping.

This week ministers from the centre-left Social Democrats (SPD), junior coalition partners to Chancellor Friedrich Merz’s conservatives, said Berlin must enshrine the need for “climate adaptation and nature conservation” in the German constitution, known as the Basic Law.

The SPD’s Environment Minister Carsten Schneider said the climate crisis was now a “tangible reality” but that current law limits what his ministry can do in response, including in helping states and local governments.

The group of ministers urged changes to urban planning legislation and building codes, and new labour laws to address working in high temperatures.

– Heat impacts hospitals, nursing homes –

The party’s former health minister, Karl Lauterbach, supported the push Thursday, arguing that municipalities need financial help to adapt to a changing climate.

“Effective heat protection costs a lot of money,” he told the Rheinische Post daily. “Many municipalities are heavily in debt and simply cannot finance the necessary measures on their own.”

Earlier this month the German Association of Towns and Municipalities argued that billions are needed to help hospitals and nursing homes, which often have no air-conditioning, adapt to scorching temperatures.

“Hospitals need air conditioning — not only for patients but also for staff,” its president Ralph Spiegler told the Rheinische Post. “We see an immense need for investment here, estimated at a minimum of 20 billion euros.”

“It is also essential to specifically address the situation in retirement and nursing homes in order to account for climate change and equip their facilities in a way that is adapted to the climate.”

Lauterbach, who has a doctoral degree in medical science, said the true number of heat deaths this year may be even higher than the statistics indicate.

“The Robert Koch Institute employs a rather conservative methodology,” he said. “This means the number of heat-related deaths is likely being underestimated.”

In general, heat-related deaths are not easily captured, he said.

“Very few people die of classic heatstroke during hot weather,” he said, with most deaths occurring in combination with other conditions.

“For instance, high heat stress can contribute to a stroke developing from pre-existing atrial fibrillation. Formally, the person might die of a stroke, but without the heat, it might not have happened.”

World.title: Alvarez ‘focused’ says new Atletico team-mate Romero
World.content:
Madrid – New Atletico Madrid defender Cristian Romero said Thursday he sees his teammate and Argentina compatriot Julian Alvarez as “really focused” and “eager to keep scoring goals” despite his attempt to leave the club.

“Julian, I see him doing very well,” Romero told reporters at his presentation after joining from Premier League side Tottenham on a five-year deal for 40 million euros ($47 million).

“I’ve been here for five or six days and I see him as always, a guy who wants to keep scoring goals, keep entertaining people, and I see him really focused.”

Amid transfer bids from Barcelona and Real Madrid, Alvarez said this summer it would be best for everyone if he was allowed to depart. However Atletico Madrid held firm and kept the former Manchester City striker.

Neither Romero or Alvarez, runners up in the World Cup, were involved in the team’s 2-0 win over Malaga on Wednesday, their La Liga opener.

Coach Diego Simeone said he would try to build the team around Alvarez, while highlighting the “leadership” of Romero, who won the World Cup with Argentina in 2022.

“(Simeone) asked me to be a leader on the pitch, to help my team-mates,” said Romero.

“I hope to be up to the challenge and carve my name into the history of this great club.”

World.title: Iran resolves banking obstacles with Iraq, plans for financial deals
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Iran and Iraq have achieved a deal to remove long-standing financial hurdles, allowing Tehran to access an estimated $11 billion in blocked oil receivables in the coming weeks.

Following the Central Bank of Iran (CBI) Governor Abdolnaser Hemmati’s high-level meetings with senior Iraqi officials in Baghdad, both countries are preparing for several critical financial and economic agreements.

The settlement followed a series of bilateral discussions between Hemmati, Central Bank of Iraq (CB) Governor Nizar Hussein, Finance Minister Faleh Sari, and Iraqi Prime Minister Ali al-Zaidi.

Al-Zaidi issued orders permitting the Iraqi government to provide guarantee letters to Iranian contractors. The step will be directly supported by Iranian assets, which are now limited in Iraqi banking institutions.

The central bank leaders developed technical frameworks to reduce currency transfer barriers and allow non-oil commerce while avoiding typical clearing constraints in the US currency.

New procedures are being adopted at border entry points to speed up cross-border logistics and payments for private companies.

For years, Iraq has relied largely on Iranian gas and energy to operate its electricity grid. However, due to rigorous US restrictions on dollar and euro transfers involving Iranian institutions, Baghdad had to deposit these oil payments into extremely restricted local financial institutions.

This limitation accumulated a debt of $10 billion to $11 billion that Tehran could not readily receive.

The new arrangements enable Baghdad to gradually decrease its debt through bartering-based payments, goods-for-debt methods, and support for internal economic initiatives.

World.title: Iraqi e-commerce startup Rozenama raises $150,000 to expand across Iraq
World.content:
Baghdad (IraqiNews.com) – Rozenama, a Baghdad-based e-commerce startup, has raised $150,000 in pre-seed capital to grow its platform and extend its services across Iraq.

Rozenama, founded in Baghdad in 2022 by Abbas Muhil and Mohammed Fawzi, offers Iraqi businesses tools for managing online shops while combining local delivery services, payment alternatives, and Iraq’s extensively utilized cash-on-delivery system.

Iraqi entrepreneur Mohammed Haider, the CEO of Aljasmi Perfumes, made the investment.

The venture is aimed at companies who still depend heavily on Instagram, WhatsApp, and other social media platforms to collect orders and manually handle sales and inventory.

Rozenama claims its active merchant base has increased from roughly 250 to more than 900 in the last year, while registered users have topped 13,000.

The extra financing will mostly go toward engineering and the launch of a refurbished version of the platform on August 25, as well as expansion into other Iraqi governorates.

The firm said that the majority of its recent growth has come from outside of Baghdad; thus, provincial markets would be a significant emphasis for its next stage.

The investment comes as Iraq’s e-commerce industry grows with the broader acceptance of digital payments, delivery services, and online shopping, opening up new prospects for locally constructed technology platforms.

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister Joseph Vijay on Thursday raised concerns over the proposed Delimitation Bill, 2026, saying southern states could lose their share of representation in Parliament if seats are redistributed mainly according to population.Speaking at the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council chaired by Union home minister Amit Shah, Vijay, who is also the council's vice-chairman, sought an assurance from the Centre that states which have successfully stabilised their populations would not be penalised through a reduction in their parliamentary representation.He said the issue had become particularly important as the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census nears its end."As the freeze on the allocation of Lok Sabha seats based on the 1971 Census approaches its end and the Delimitation Bill, 2026, is considered, there is a genuine and shared concern across the Southern States that delimitation based predominantly on populations may diminish our collective voice in Parliament," he said.Vijay argued that southern states had achieved population control while also making progress in human development and economic growth.He said these achievements should not result in the states receiving less political representation."The Southern States have been at the forefront of population stabilisation, human development, and economic growth. These achievements reflect the successful implementation of national priorities and should not result in a reduction of our representation. Public policy must not inadvertently penalise States for fulfilling national objectives," he said.He called for a legislative guarantee to ensure that the proportion of parliamentary seats held by any state would not fall because of its success in controlling population growth."I therefore, urge the Union Government to provide a clear legislative assurance that no State will suffer a reduction in its percentage of representation in Parliament on account of its success in population stabilisation. Such an approach would uphold the principles of equity, preserve the federal balance envisioned by our Constitution, and reinforce the confidence of all States in our democratic institutions," he added.Southern states, particularly Tamil Nadu and Kerala, have for years raised concerns about a population-based delimitation exercise.Their argument is that these states followed national family planning and population control policies more successfully over the past five decades. As a result, their populations have grown at a slower rate than those of several northern states.Vijay also raised the issue of inter-state river disputes, with particular focus on the long-running Cauvery dispute between Tamil Nadu and Karnataka.He said cooperation between states was important but must go hand in hand with compliance with court orders and decisions of statutory bodies."Water is fundamental to the lives, Agriculture and livelihoods of millions, and the management of interstate rivers demands both cooperation and unwavering respect for the rule of law. First, the legitimate rights of lower riparian States and the livelihoods that depend on assured river flows must be fully protected. Second, the judgments of the Supreme Court, the awards of duly constituted tribunals, and the statutory mechanisms established for river management must be implemented in letter and spirit," he said.Referring specifically to the Cauvery dispute, Vijay said decisions taken by the Supreme Court and the Cauvery Water Management Authority must be implemented without delay."The timely implementation of the Supreme Court's judgment and the decisions of the Cauvery Water Management Authority remains essential," he said.The Cauvery Water Management Authority had directed Karnataka to release 12,000 cusecs of water a day to Tamil Nadu at Biligundlu from 8 am on August 12 for 15 days. The Supreme Court has also directed the Karnataka government to ensure compliance with the order.Vijay also reiterated Tamil Nadu's opposition to the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test, or NEET, saying the examination places rural and disadvantaged students at a disadvantage."Tamil Nadu has consistently maintained that the National Eligibility cum Entrance Test (NEET) places students from rural backgrounds and socially and economically disadvantaged communities at a distinct disadvantage, undermining the State's long-standing model of inclusive access based on school education," he said.He asked the Centre to allow Tamil Nadu to use Class XII marks to fill medical seats reserved under the state quota."I urge the Union Government to permit Tamil Nadu to fill all seats under the State quota in MBBS, BDS, and AYUSH courses solely based on Class XII marks, in keeping with the State's proven and equitable admission system," he said.Vijay also called for stronger regulation of the online sale of prescription medicines and greater coordination between states to tackle the illegal drug trade and substance abuse."I urge the Government of India to strengthen the regulatory framework governing the online sale of prescription medicines, ensure stricter enforcement against their unauthorised sale, and review the existing legal framework to effectively address emerging substance abuse among youth," he said.

World.title: Amit Shah hails South's development in CMs meet, cites 3 pillars of progress
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Union home minister

on Thursday hailed the development journey of the southern states, saying "high literacy rate, trained manpower and technical expertise in the utilisation of deep seas" have been the three pillars behind the progess of these states.

Chairing the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council in

's Mahabalipuram, the Union home minister said: "The people of South India and the governments have also established many excellent traditions in the fields of innovation and revenue generation."

He said that "the whole of India should learn from South India in these two areas," as per the home ministery's statement.

Amit Shah on Thursday chaired the 31st meeting of the Southern Zonal Council at a private star hotel in Kovalam near Mamallapuram, where leaders and senior officials from southern states discussed inter-state disputes, security concerns and development priorities.

Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay, who serves as the council's vice-chairman, personally welcomed Shah upon his arrival. The two leaders also held a brief interaction before the meeting began. During the proceedings, Vijay was seated alongside Karnataka chief minister DK Shivakumar.

Representatives from Tamil Nadu, Andhra Pradesh, Karnataka, Kerala and Telangana took part in the meeting.

World.title: Battle for UP's 'Aadhi Aabadi': Why parties are wooing women voters like never before ahead of 2027 polls
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Uttar Pradesh elections have traditionally been about the caste arithmetic: counting Yadavs, non-Yadav OBCs, Dalits, Brahmins and Muslims. But ahead of the 2027 battle, there is another constituency the parties simply cannot afford to ignore: the women voters - who transcend the caste divide.

Every election cycle, the same questions return: Can the BJP retain its non-Yadav OBC votes? Will Akhilesh Yadav manage to woo Brahmins and Dalits? Which side will the Jatav voters pick? Will Mayawati be able to rally all Dalits behind her BSP? And so on.

This time around, while the caste questions remain, the battle will also be for the support of Uttar Pradesh's 'Aadhi Aabadi' - the women voters who have proved to be game changers, election after election in many other states.

When Uttar Pradesh votes in 2027 to elect a new assembly, the state's 6,09,09,525 female voters, who constitute 45.46% of the total electorate, will hold considerable sway over the fortunes of the political contenders.

That explains why Yogi Adityanath and Akhilesh Yadav, the two key challengers, are leaving no stone unturned to bring women into their fold. Congress, too, is preparing to step up its outreach as the electoral battle gathers pace.





Why women voters matter

Let's rewind to 2007. In the 2007 UP assembly election, the female turnout in the state was under 42%, less than the male turnout of 49.35%.

But this changed five years later. In 2012, Uttar Pradesh had around 5.72 crore registered women voters, of whom 3.45 crore cast their ballots. Thus, the female turnout increased to around 60.3%, surpassing that of males at about 58.7%.

By the 2017 assembly election, the number of registered women voters had gone up to 6.46 crore.

More than 4.09 crore women voted, and female turnout climbed to around 63.4% while the men lagged at 59%.

In 2022, Uttar Pradesh had around 7.02 crore women electors, out of which more than 4.36 crore voted. Female turnout stood at around 62.2%, once again higher than that among men, which stood at around 59.6%.

So, between 2012 and 2022 alone, the state added nearly 1.3 crore women to its electoral rolls. But what may be more important for political parties is the fact that 2012 elections onwards women outvoted men in all assembly elections in the state.

The 2024 Lok Sabha election was no different.

In Uttar Pradesh, 57.22% of women electors turned out to vote in the 2024 general elections, compared to 56.46% of men. The overall turnout was lower than in the recent assembly elections, but women still maintained their lead.

And itâs not just UP. Parties cannot ignore the decisive role women voters have played in assembly elections in Bihar, Maharashtra, West Bengal, Madhya Pradesh and Jharkhand.

Ahead of the assembly election in Madhya Pradesh, the Shivraj Singh Chouhan government rolled out the 'Ladli Behna' programme, a monthly cash assistance scheme under which money was transferred directly into women's accounts. By the time Madhya Pradesh voted, the scheme covered more than a crore women. BJP won 163 of the 230 seats. 'Ladli Behna' quickly became one of the key takeaways from the election.

Maharashtra also introduced its own version: the 'Ladki Bahin' programme.

And then Bihar happened. The 2025 assembly election recorded a female turnout of 71.6%. Male turnout was 62.8%. The NDA went on to win a huge majority.

How parties are wooing women voters

Financial doles under DBT (Direct Benefit Transfer) no longer make news. If the elections are round the corner, they are a given. What makes news is the amount of dole.

So, when some media reports suggested that the Yogi Adityanath government was considering a dole of Rs 50,000 for women ahead of elections - Rs 20,000 now and Rs 30,000 after its return to power - Akhilesh Yadav lost no time to dish out a pre-election offer to counter the BJP.

âWe will start with Rs 40,000 and increase it every year,â the SP chief wrote in a post on X while questioning the BJPâs intent and alleging that the BJP was distributing "the earnings of its sins.

"

Akhilesh simultaneously launched a broadside against the BJP and alleged that the party has been left with "nothing but money" to win the 2027 Uttar Pradesh Assembly elections. âThe religious women of UP will never accept the ill-gotten money of the BJP,â the SP chief wrote.

He also tried to discredit the BJP and claimed that the party was not keeping its promise of giving the announced doles to women in other states where it governed.

"The BJP's corrupt government has eaten up Rs 5 lakh belonging to women over the last 10 years and is now serving the jumla of giving only Rs 20,000. Rs 20,000 is only four per cent of Rs 5 lakh, which means these BJP people have swallowed 96 per cent of women's share," he alleged.

BJP Uttar Pradesh vice-president Neeraj Singh hit back at Akhilesh, saying his party has made no such announcement and accused the SP chief of making a "deceptive" promise to give Rs 40,000 to women.

"Whenever the BJP provides benefits under its schemes to eligible people, the important thing is that the money reaches those who are entitled to it. The distribution system is also very transparent, and this has been the BJP's track record," the BJP leader claimed.

On the SP's promise of Rs 40,000 annually to women, Singh said it was "only a deception" and alleged that the party had used a similar tactic before the 2024 Lok Sabha elections.

But while the BJP questions Akhilesh Yadavâs sincerity, it perhaps realises that the SP chief has raised the bar and also the expectation of women in the state by announcing a dole of Rs 40,000, and this announcement may influence whatever dole the ruling party eventually decides.

Akhilesh may have scored some brownie points here, but the fact remains that the SP chief faces a tough challenge from the BJP in UP. Chief minister Yogi Adityanath has been in a relentless pursuit of women voters, announcing a string of programmes for them at regular intervals.

In March, Yogi Adityanath distributed smartphones to 69,804 Anganwadi workers and supervisors, over two lakh growth monitoring devices, and appointment letters to 18,440 Anganwadi workers and helpers.

Addressing the gathering, he said, "If the newborn is well-nourished and the mother is healthy, the future of India will be strong."

In April, the Uttar Pradesh government launched a one-of-its-kind scheme titled 'Safe Mobility Program,' centred around employment generation for female members of Self-Help Groups (SHGs). Under the programme, an army of female e-rickshaw pilots will be trained across the state to ensure safe, accessible, and dignified transportation for girls and women travelling to schools, workplaces, and other essential destinations.

From April 16 to 20, the Yogi government ran a five-day special campaign under the Nari Shakti Vandan Abhiyan to turn schools into active centres of women empowerment, focusing on building confidence, leadership qualities, and awareness among girl students.

In another move to support and prop up 'naari shakti', the Uttar Pradesh government directed sugarcane co-operative societies in the state to allocate free spaces to women from Self Help Groups (SHGs) to set up their shops.

The idea was to encourage women from SHGs to start âPrerna canteensâ from here, displaying and selling their products.

These are some examples that showcase how Yogi Adityanath has been mindful of the power of women voters in the 2027 battle and has been working to reach out to them through his welfare measures.

Congress's another shot at wooing women voters

BJP and

are not the only parties to target this demographic. Congress had, in fact, put women at the centre of its Uttar Pradesh campaign much before the current race over cash transfers began.

In 2022, Priyanka Gandhi Vadra, who was the general secretary of the All India Congress Committee (AICC) in charge of Uttar Pradesh back then, led the party's 'Ladki Hoon, Lad Sakti Hoon' campaign. The party took a bold gamble by promising to give 40% of assembly tickets to women.

The party eventually fielded a large number of women candidates and also made promises aimed specifically at female voters, including smartphones for girls and electric scooters for female students.

However, that move did not pay off. Congress won just two of the 403 assembly seats and its vote share slipped to around 2.3%.

The situation, however, is different going into 2027. Congress won six Lok Sabha seats in Uttar Pradesh in 2024 as part of its alliance with the Samajwadi Party, which won 37. The opposition therefore enters the assembly battle with more political space than it had in 2022. For Congress, the challenge will be to revive its women outreach and aim to translate schemes into electoral benefit.

Women are voting more, but are they voting as one bloc?

But amid all the attention on cash transfers and the push for women-centric schemes, the question that remains is: Can women's votes be treated as one single bloc? A Jatav woman, a Muslim woman, a non-Yadav OBC woman may have very different expectations when she enters the polling booth to cast her vote. Caste, religion and past preferences may still continue to matter, as will factors like inflation, jobs, law and order, women's safety, welfare benefits and the candidate on the ground.

Join conversation Commentsâ Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

Therefore, it is hard to predict if the high turnout among women can automatically translate into an advantage for any one party.

But what it does surely mean is that no party can afford to take the 'Aadhi Aabadi' for granted anymore. When it comes to voting, women have outperformed men in the last three Uttar Pradesh assembly elections and have maintained that lead in the 2024 Lok Sabha polls as well. So, while caste will always play a role in UP elections, the 2027 battle will also come down to who wins the trust of the over six crore women voters. The question is no longer whether women will turn up to vote.

It is: who will they vote for?

World.title: 'Provide proof or apologise': BJP to opposition over Nitin Nabin's 'non-vegetarian' meal claim
World.content:
NEW DELHI: Bharatiya Janata Party on Thursday demanded that Congress and Samajwadi Party provide proof or issue a public apology for claiming that saffron party president Nitin Nabin consumed non-vegetarian food during the ongoing Hindu holy month of Sawan.

In a social media post on X, BJP said that Nabin, during his visit to Andhra Pradesh, ate 100 percent vegetarian local dishes, including raw jackfruit curry.

Slamming the opposition, BJP said that the accusation stems from the "lack of awareness about South Indian cuisine."

"If you have made an allegation, provide proof, or apologise! During his Andhra Pradesh visit, BJP national president Shri Nitin Nabin ate traditional local 100 percent vegetarian dishes, including raw jackfruit curry (Panasa Mukkalu)," BJP said.

"However, Congress, Samajwadi Party and their ecosystem are spreading false claims, without verification, that the food was non-vegetarian. The opposition's claim, which stems from a lack of awareness about South Indian cuisine, was exposed within a few hours. Now the direct question: Provide proof of the allegation or publicly apologise to the country. Politics should be based on truth, not lies!" it added.

This comes after Congress and Samajwadi Party took a swipe at Nabin over a video showing him and other party leaders having a meal at a recent event in Andhra Pradesh.





The opposition parties claimed that the leaders were seen eating non-vegetarian food.

In a social media post on X, Chhattisgarh Congress had shared the video and said, "Sanatan on the face, values in speechesâ¦ the rest is evident from BJP's conduct."

World.title: 'UGC regulation under reconsideration', govt tells SC on controversial equity rules
World.content:
The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the Supreme Court on January 29.

SC had earlier put regulations on hold

Court questioned provisions on caste discrimination

Join conversation View All Comments â Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful Â· TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Centre on Thursday informed the Supreme Court that the 2026 University Grants Commission (UGC) equity regulations, which seek to address caste-based discrimination in higher education institutions, are currently being reconsidered.The development came during a hearing before a bench comprising Chief Justice Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana. The court was hearing several petitions challenging the validity of the regulations."This is the UGC regulation matter. It is under reconsideration," Solicitor General Tushar Mehta told the bench.The Supreme Court subsequently directed the UGC to submit a comprehensive counter affidavit within four weeks. The petitioners will have two weeks after that to file their rejoinders, if any.The 2026 regulations had already been kept in abeyance by the top court on January 29. At the time, the court said the provisions were "prima facie vague" and could have "very sweeping consequences", warning that they could potentially divide society and have a "dangerous impact".The court had also asked the Centre and the UGC to respond to three petitions challenging the new framework."In exercise of our powers under Article 142 of the Constitution, we further direct that the University Grants Commission (Promotion of Equity in Higher Education Institutions) Regulations, 2012, will continue to operate and remain in force till further orders," it had said.The regulations had faced opposition in several places, with student groups and other organisations calling for their immediate withdrawal.While examining the regulations, the Supreme Court raised questions about how some of their provisions were framed.One concern related to Regulation 3(1)(c), which separately defines "caste-based discrimination". The court questioned why a separate definition was necessary when Regulation 3(1)(e) already contains a broader definition of "discrimination".The bench also questioned the exclusion of ragging from the regulations, noting that it remains a common form of harassment in educational institutions.The court had further observed that the wording of the 2026 regulations appeared "prima facie vague" and "capable of misuse".Advocate Vishnu Shankar Jain, representing one of the petitioners, had challenged Regulation 3(1)(c). The provision defines caste-based discrimination as discrimination "only on the basis of caste or tribe" against members of Scheduled Castes, Scheduled Tribes and Other Backward Classes.

World.title: NEET protests: SC sets up 5-member panel to probe excessive use of force by cops on students
World.content:
NEW DELHI: A day after the

announced it will be setting up a committee to examine allegations of excessive use of force by security personnel against students during the July 20 student march over the NEET paper leak, the top court on Thursday said that a five-member panel will be headed by former SC judge Justice R Subhash Reddy.

Other members of the committee include former Punjab and Haryana high court Chief Justice Ravi Shankar Jha, former Delhi high court judge Justice Shalinder Kaur, former CBI director Rishi Kumar Shukla and retired Meghalaya Director General of Police Dr LR Bishnoi.

The committee will examine allegations of excessive use of pellet guns, electric batons, lathi charges and tear gas, along with alleged violence against women protesters.

It will also look into police surveillance, the proportionality of crowd-control measures, and the provision of medical assistance and compensation to victims. The committee will also consider allegations by authorities of violence against police personnel and damage to public property.

This comes as the apex court is hearing a batch of petitions alleging excessive police action against students who participated in protests at Jantar Mantar and other locations across the country over alleged NEET examination paper leaks and broader concerns relating to the examination system.





The proceedings come against the backdrop of weeks of student demonstrations led by the Cockroach Janata Party (CJP) at Jantar Mantar, including a hunger strike and a subsequent march towards Parliament.

On July 20, thousands of students participated in a Parliament march organised by the CJP, demanding, among other things, the resignation of Union education minister Dharmendra Pradhan over alleged examination paper leaks and seeking wider reforms in the examination system.

The Delhi Police, however, defended its action and maintained that force was used only after sections of the protesting crowd allegedly turned violent and engaged in stone-pelting.

As part of Corporate Social Responsibility(CSR) initiative, officials of the South Asia LPG Company provided artificial limbs to 350 needy physically challenged persons at a programme organised at the Sri Gurudeva Charitable Trust of Mangalampalem, Kothavalasa mandal in Vizianagaram district on Thursday. World.title: ‘Public can draw essential commodities at fair price shops by providing family card number, biometrics’
World.content:
Minister for Food and Civil Supplies P. Venkataramanan on Thursday said that the original smart cards need not be produced to draw essential commodities at fair price shops in the State. It would be enough if a digital copy is shown or number is given along with the biometric data by the card holder.

Speaking on the demands for the Food department in the State Assembly, he said that card holders can draw commodities at any shop of their choice. "Suppose someone is travelling, they can draw their essential goods from a shop in the vicinity," he explained.

MLAs including S. Kamaraj of Mannargudi and K. Karthikeyan of Kallakurichi expressed concerns over lack of internet connectivity at fair price shops in far flung areas of their constituencies. Mr. Kamaraj wanted to know if the old method of just issuing bills for the goods could be opted in such locations. "In the Kalvaroyan Hills, the scanning devices keep lagging. Nearly 25% of my population lives in the hills," said Mr. Karthikeyan.

Later, the Minister announced that as part of the government's efforts to augment storage capacity for food grains, 15 godowns will be constructed in 13 districts at a total cost of ₹81.60 crore. He said the combined capacity of these facilities would be 31,000 tonnes and they would be for use of the Tamil Nadu Civil Supplies Corporation.

They would come up in districts including Chengalpattu, Cuddalore, Salem, Kancheepuram, Kallakurichi, Tirunelveli, Thanjavur, Karur, Coimbatore, Thenkasi, Salem, Sivagangai and Namakkal. The warehouses would have drinking water and toilet facilities for staff too.

The Minister also announced the construction of three modern godowns at the existing storage premises' belonging to the Tamil Nadu Warehouse Corporation at Ariyalur, Namakkal and Mettupalayam at a cost of ₹13.50 crore with a combined capacity of 3400 tonnes. Maintenance of 17 existing godowns belonging to the corporation would be taken up at a cost of ₹12.61 crore.

Mr. Venkataramanan said that lands belonging to the Dharmapuram Aadheenam were being used to create additional storage for food grains. Steps would be taken to prevent loaders from collecting ₹50 per bag of paddy from farmers at the direct procurement centres.

World.title: Dispose 22-A complaints expeditiously, says Ponguleti
World.content:
Minister for Revenue Ponguleti Srinivas Reddy directed officials to treat every complaint received through the 22-A prohibited lands call centre as a responsibility and ensure that it was monitored until its final resolution.

Reviewing the functioning of the call centre and the status of 22-A-related applications through a teleconference with officials, the Minister assured the genuine title holders that the government would stand by them.

Officials informed the Minister that around 400 calls had been received by the call centre so far. He reviewed the complaints being received, their disposal, and the nature of the issues being raised. He also sought details of the status of 22-A applications in four districts.

Mr. Srinivas Reddy directed officials to immediately forward the complete details of every complaint received through the call centre to the concerned tahsildar, RDO, sub-registrar and other officials.

The Minister directed sub-registrars, tahsildars, RDOs and Collectors to take up both pending applications and those received over the past two or three days and dispose of them immediately.

“A person visiting a revenue office should leave with the confidence that his problem will be resolved,” he told officials. He also cautioned officials against taking decisions on their own that could cause hardship to people.

World.title: Tenkasi Collector orders closure of garbage yard
World.content:
Collector Ranjeet Singh on Thursday ordered the closure of Boganallur garbage yard, where Tenkasi and Kadayanallur municipalities dumped waste generated under their jurisdiction.

The decision was taken after inmates of the Boganallur Sri Lankan Tamil refugees rehabilitation camp submitted a petition with the Collector on Monday, seeking closure of the garbage yard that posed serious health hazards to the camp. Two ’ residents, a 13-year-old girl and a 27-year-old woman, who were suffering from a ‘mysterious fever’, died in the past 30 days, they said.

Following the deaths, which were allegedly caused by dengue according to the families of the deceased, Mr. Ranjeet Singh paid a surprise visit to the camp on Thursday to check the complaints of the residents. He also met other residents living near the garbage yard.

As the public and the inmates of the rehabilitation camp unanimously objected to the dumping of garbage near their houses, Mr. Ranjeet Singh visited the garbage yard also. After ordering the closure of the garbage yard, the Collector visited the camp again and ordered the officials of the Public Health Department to organise medical camps there until the last fever case was treated.

He instructed the doctors in the special camp to screen all inmates for other ailments also as a precautionary measure. “Those who need further medical attention should be referred to Tirunelveli Medical College Hospital,” he said.

The Collector asked the medical officers to submit a comprehensive report on the special medical camp conducted in the rehabilitation camp so as to take appropriate remedial measures.

World.title: Man held for allegedly circulating morphed images of Thangal
World.content:
The police at Tirurangadi arrested a man for allegedly circulating derogatory posters and morphed images of Indian Union Muslim League (IUML) State president Syed Sadikali Shihab Thangal on social media.

The arrested person was identified as Ponniyath Anvar from Velliyamburam, Nannambra. The case was registered on a complaint by U.A. Razak, Muslim Youth League president of the Tirurangadi constituency.

According to the complaint, morphed images of Mr. Thangal were circulated through a WhatsApp group named ‘Nannambra Politics’, along with obscene and abusive remarks.

The complaint alleged that such posts could lead to communal tensions and clashes in the area.

According to the first information report, Anvar was booked for allegedly attempting to incite a riot by circulating defamatory content. An investigation is under way.

World.title: Health department observes World Mosquito Day with intensive vector-control drives across Keralam
World.content:
The Keralam Health department observed World Mosquito Day on Thursday (August 20, 2026) with a renewed call to launch awareness programmes and intensive control measures to check mosquito population in the State.

It has called upon households, institutions and the community to work together to eliminate mosquito-breeding sources so that the State has a better grip on the vector-borne diseases that affect a significant proportion of the population every year.

Health Minister K. Muraleedharan inaugurated the World Mosquito Day observance on Thursday (August 20, 2026) at Vattiyurkavu, his constituency, which has become one of the major hotspots for mosquito-borne diseases such as dengue and chikungunya in the district this season.

Despite extensive surveillance and vector-control machinery, mosquito-borne diseases remain stubbornly entrenched in the State.

Though the State reports several mosquito-borne diseases like malaria, filariasis, West Nile, Japanese encephalitis and chikungunya, the challenge is particularly acute with dengue.

108 species in State

A study published in Nature in August 2025, which conducted extensive entomological surveys in five districts—Wayanad, Ernakulam, Pathanamthitta, Idukki and Thiruvananthapuram—had reported that the State was home to 108 species of mosquitoes.

Researchers identified 14 established species which are known disease-vectors, and also found several species of the Aedes albopictus mosquito whose disease-transmission potential remains unknown. In all five districts, Aedes albopictus seemed to be the dominant vector. However, by its sheer number, A. aegypti continues to be the primary dengue vector.

The study reiterated what is already known, that artificial man-made habitats—discarded plastic containers, tyres, flower pots and other waste materials like coconut shells thrown away carelessly—contributed substantially to the number and diversity of mosquitoes.

This underlines how human activity is enhancing environmental factors and climate, which already favours the explosive growth in mosquito population.

The focus of mosquito control continues to be source reduction or elimination of breeding grounds, which should be an intensive activity around individual households, with every urban resident taking up the responsibility of keeping one’s house and surroundings free of breeding opportunities for mosquitoes, health officials said.

Construction sites or blocked drains in a vacant property can all be breeding grounds for Aedes species. Hence the health administration is planning intensive disease surveillance and control measures around known hotspots and migrant labour camps.

Continuous community-level elimination of breeding sites should be sustained through the year as the State has two heavy monsoon seasons as well as intermittent rainfall. Intermittent rainfall followed by warm spells accelerates the mosquito breeding pace, something that Thiruvananthapuram in particular has witnessed this season.

World Mosquito Day is being used as an opportunity by the Health department to take the conversation about dengue to the entire community, so that local bodies, residents’ associations, construction workers, schools and institutions also play a role in keeping the vector indices down.

World.title: Telangana High Court takes serious note of government affidavit wrongly quoting Article 162 in welfare schemes case
World.content:
Justice N.V. Shravan Kumar of the Telangana High Court on Thursday took a serious note of the State government’s affidavit, in which Article 162 of the Constitution of India was wrongly quoted, filed in the High Court seeking vacation of the order staying Kalyana Lakshmi and Shaadi Mubarak schemes’ operation.

The affidavit filed by B. Bala Maya Devi, Principal Secretary to Government (Full Additional Charge), Backward Classes Welfare Department, stated that the impugned G.O.s relating to implementation of the two welfare schemes were issued under Article 162 of the Constitution to achieve the constitutional goals of social justice. The affidavit also stated that under Article 162 the executive power of a State is completely co-extensive and co-terminus with its legislative competence.

When the judge sought to know if the Article 162 mentioned in the affidavit was correct, the Additional Advocate General Mohammed Imran Khan admitted that it was wrongly mentioned describing it as a typographical error. The AAG said that the part of 162 Article quoted in the affidavit was not only a mistake but a blunder. The judge directed the AAG to file a rectified affidavit.

Before directing the Finance Secretary to file an affidavit on the status of the government taking loans to continue welfare schemes, the judge also asked the AAG what was the priority of the government when it comes to discharging statutory obligations like paying compensation to land losers and welfare schemes. Justice Shravan Kumar said some staff members of Mahbubnagar court (the judge’s administrative court) did not get salaries for four months.

The judge made it clear that it was not for the courts to interfere on how the government dealt with the finances. But the courts had to maintain a balance in deciding matters relating to finance administration, he said. The AAG, however, raised objection over advocate Vijay Gopal -who filed the writ petition challenging the constitutional validity of implementation of the two schemes- reading out the representation of some retired government employees not receiving their post-retirement benefits for months together.

While the AAG said it amounted to making political statements in the open court, the petitioner and advocate contended that he was only attempting to bring to attention of the court as to how debts due to welfare schemes were affecting State’s discharge of statutory obligations. The matter was posted to Monday for next hearing.

World.title: Devaraj Urs’s Jayanthi celebrated in Mysuru
World.content:
Glowing tributes were offered to former Chief Minister D. Devaraj Urs on his 111th birth anniversary in Mysuru on Thursday.

Deputy Commissioner of Mysuru G. Lakshmikant Reddy, Mysuru Zilla Panchayat Chief Executive Officer S. Yukesh Kumar and Mysuru City Corporation (MCC) Commissioner M.K. Savitha were among the officials, who showered flower petals on the newly installed statue of Urs in the Deputy Commissioner’s office in Siddhartha Nagar.

Chairman of Mysore Paints and Varnishes Limited H.D. Ganesh inaugurated the 111th birth anniversary celebrations organised by the Mysuru district administration, Mysuru Zilla Panchayat, MCC and Department of Backward Classes Welfare at Kalamandira in the City.

Speaking on the occasion, Mr. Ganesh said the ideals and vision of Urs, who provided efficient and honest administration for eight years, would continue to guide the younger generation.

“While some people read history, there are some who create history. This statement applies to D. Devaraj Urs,” Mr. Ganesh said.

He said Urs was a great leader who did not seek power for his own sake, but for supporting the lives of the disadvantaged and ensuring justice for backward communities.

MCC Commissioner M.K. Savitha said D. Devaraj Urs had made immense contributions to the uplift of backward classes.

Mr. Urs worked with the objective of ensuring that power and rights reached even the most disadvantaged sections of society, she said. Through the land reforms legislation and the “land to the tiller” initiative, he provided economic and social security to oppressed sections, she added.

He also laid the foundation for an educational transformation by establishing hostels for students belonging to backward classes and Scheduled Castes and Scheduled Tribes.

Speaking on the occasion, Halappa H., a lecturer at the Government Pre-University College in Saragur, said Urs viewed power not merely as an instrument of administration but as a responsibility to bring about a transformation in the lives of the disadvantaged and the most marginalised sections of society.

Mr. Lakshmikanth Reddy, Mr Yukesh Kumar, Mysuru District Backward Classes Welfare Officer Raghavendra, Taluk Backward Classes Welfare Officer Rekha B.C., officials of the Backward Classes Welfare Department and students were among those present.

World.title: PM Shehbaz stresses need to translate friendship with Syria into bilateral cooperation
World.content:
Visiting Syrian Foreign Minister Asaad Hassan al-Shaibani met Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif on Thursday, with the premier stressing that the longstanding ties between Islamabad and Damascus needed to yield enhanced bilateral cooperation, according to a statement from the Prime Minister’s Office (PMO).

Damascus’ top diplomat arrived in Islamabad in the early hours for an official visit at the invitation of Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Ishaq Dar.
